what_happened.summary: Being hit by a pitch and going hitless can feel scary and heavy for an 11-year-old, but those moments are information, not a definition of who he is. The one focus this week is building confidence through safe contact reps and praising what he controls: being ready, his approach, and his effort rather than hits. This guidance comes from draft coaching notes that haven't been reviewed yet.

output.call_type_rationale: The appropriate response follows from baseball rules and coaching guidelines once the facts of the hit-by-pitch occurrences and the player's fear are known, rather than relying on an umpire's real-time judgment.

channel.who: You, the head coach, and the player's parents
channel.how: Talk to the player one-on-one calmly before or after practice, not mid-game; ask parents to let the player talk first after games, praise effort and approach, and leave hitting mechanics to you at a calm, agreed time.

output.teachable_moment: A hit by pitch or an out doesn't determine his value; what matters is how he prepares, competes, and responds one pitch at a time.

individual: Take five quality two-strike tee reps on the outer half each practice, driving the ball the other way with a helmet on every swing.
After each at-bat, name one controllable he did well ready, approach, effort before talking about the result.
team: Run tee and soft-toss rounds in a safe net so he gets confident contact reps without live pitching at first.
Praise process out loud in practice great approach, you were ready instead of only celebrating hits.
at_home: Ask him how the at-bat felt and what he learned, praise his effort and courage, and leave swing mechanics to the coach.
Keep it low-pressure and fun; let him talk first after a tough game.

output.focus: Build confidence through safe contact reps and process praise

life_lesson.text: Believe in him before he believes in himself, and remind him his worth isn't his stat line. That steady belief helps a player at school, at work, and at home, not just on the diamond.

lessons.title: Believe in your players before they believe in themselves
lessons.principle: Have confidence in your players even when they don't show it, even when their track record says failure. Don't lose that confidence. Feed it to them and they will succeed.

lessons.title: Your value isn't your stat line
lessons.principle: Your value is not determined by your failures or your successes.

recalled.content: The player is working on recovering from a game-ending strikeout.
The player is age 10 and plays baseball.
